expected_behaviors: Maintains continuity with the exact experiment.
Distinguishes MIDI event, region, track, channel strip, file, output, freeze, bounce, and latency ownership.
Recommends at most one next experiment.
Preserves baseline, stop condition, undo, and version-scoped guidance.
Explains the transferable Logic principle naturally.
forbidden_behaviors: Claims to have seen, heard, changed, bounced, frozen, deleted, or verified Logic without current evidence.
Treats one export, snap, CC, buffer, or PDC setting as universally correct.
Restarts from a generic checklist without referencing the prior test.

messages.text: What should I understand about MIDI Controller Events Beyond Notes, and what does it actually affect in Logic Pro?

Clarify only ownership or scope that changes the next move, then present one reversible experiment: Duplicate the MIDI region, open an event view that exposes non-note data, filter to one controller type, and compare playback before changing anything.
That helped, but now another part of the performance, routing, timing, or editability feels worse.
Reference the exact prior test, state what the result strengthens or rules out, and recommend at most one next experiment.
Why did that happen, and what should I learn from it?

Explain naturally and connect the lesson to this principle: MIDI regions can contain notes plus control change, pitch bend, aftertouch, and other events; the event type, channel, time, and value determine what the instrument receives.
